# Tool reference

83 tools, all served by `darkroom mcp`. Every call is validated, journaled once (also on failure) and returned as JSON. Edit tools work on a virtual copy of the photo, never the original file, inside the guardrail limits (see `DESIGN.md`).

| Tool | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`get_app_status`](#get_app_status) | reads | Check whether Lightroom Classic and Photoshop are running and ready to be used. |
| [`get_capabilities`](#get_capabilities) | reads | Report the installed Lightroom Classic, plug-in and Photoshop versions, whether each is a version darkroom_ai was tested with, and which features are verified, untested, have a known issue or are unavailable. |
| [`run_selftest`](#run_selftest) | reads | Check, probe by probe, that the installed Lightroom Classic (and Photoshop, if it is already running) still behaves as darkroom_ai expects: versions, catalog read, every Develop key the tools use (drift check), metadata, presets, preview. |
| [`ensure_apps_running`](#ensure_apps_running) | reads | Start Lightroom Classic or Photoshop if it is not running, and wait until it answers. |
| [`get_photo_info`](#get_photo_info) | reads | Read facts about a photo and its current basic settings. |
| [`list_catalog_photos`](#list_catalog_photos) | reads | List photos in the open Lightroom catalog, one page at a time, with their ids and camera/lens/exposure facts. |
| [`catalog_summary`](#catalog_summary) | reads | Summarise the whole catalog: how many photos, and counts by camera, lens, ISO band, file format, star rating, capture year and folder. |
| [`list_catalogs`](#list_catalogs) | reads | List the Lightroom catalogs (.lrcat files) found on this PC, say which one is open now and which ones darkroom_ai is allowed to change. |
| [`get_catalog_info`](#get_catalog_info) | reads | Describe the catalog that is open in Lightroom now: how many photos, virtual copies and keywords, the collection tree with counts, the folder tree with counts, whether darkroom_ai may change it, and which catalogs and photo folders the owner has allowed. |
| [`request_catalog_access`](#request_catalog_access) | writes | Ask the OWNER to allow darkroom_ai to change a catalog (and optionally the photo folders it uses). |
| [`request_folder_access`](#request_folder_access) | writes | Ask the OWNER to allow darkroom_ai to import from and edit photos in a folder (for example the folder they just gave you). |
| [`create_collection_set`](#create_collection_set) | writes | Create a collection set (a folder for collections) in the open catalog. |
| [`create_collection`](#create_collection) | writes | Create a collection in the open catalog. |
| [`add_to_collection`](#add_to_collection) | writes | Add photos (masters or virtual copies) to an existing collection. |
| [`remove_from_collection`](#remove_from_collection) | writes | Remove photos from a collection (the photos stay in the catalog). |
| [`get_collection_photos`](#get_collection_photos) | reads | List the photos in one collection (ids and file names, at most 200). |
| [`create_keyword`](#create_keyword) | writes | Create a keyword, or a keyword hierarchy ("Places/Japan/Kyoto"), in the catalog. |
| [`undo_collection_change`](#undo_collection_change) | writes | Take back darkroom_ai's collection changes made in THIS session (adds, removes, created collections and sets). |
| [`scan_folder`](#scan_folder) | reads | Say what importing a folder would add to the catalog (new photos, already-present photos, unsupported files) without changing anything. |
| [`import_folder`](#import_folder) | writes | Add the photos in a folder to the catalog WITHOUT moving, copying or changing any file. |
| [`get_photo_metadata`](#get_photo_metadata) | reads | Read the camera, lens and exposure facts of a photo (make, model, lens, focal length, aperture, shutter speed, ISO, capture time, size, file type). |
| [`get_selected_photos`](#get_selected_photos) | reads | List the photo(s) selected in Lightroom Classic, with their catalog ids. |
| [`find_photo`](#find_photo) | reads | Find a photo in the open catalog by its file path and return its catalog id. |
| [`get_preview`](#get_preview) | reads | Render the photo as Lightroom shows it right now and return the picture itself, so you can look at it. |
| [`analyze_photo`](#analyze_photo) | reads | Export a small preview and measure it: tones, clipping, colour cast, faces if available. |
| [`analyze_batch`](#analyze_batch) | reads | Measure many photos in one call and return a few numbers per photo (tones, clipping, colour cast). |
| [`measure_region`](#measure_region) | reads | Measure the colour and brightness of up to 6 rectangles of a photo as numbers (CIELAB lightness, a*, b*, hue angle, chroma, median RGB, clipping). |
| [`plan_crop`](#plan_crop) | reads | Work out the largest crop with a given shape (aspect ratio) that stays inside the picture after rotating it by `angle` degrees, as numbers for the `crop` tool. |
| [`view_region`](#view_region) | reads | Make a close-up picture of part of the photo as it is now, so you can look at it with your image viewer (for example a face, a shadow edge or a spot). |
| [`zone_map`](#zone_map) | reads | Map brightness over the photo: a grid of cells (mean luma, tonal zone 0-10, clipping) and the connected dark regions with their box, area, how much darker than their surroundings they are, and how hard their edge is (a hard edge behind a subject is typical of flash shadows). |
| [`find_candidates`](#find_candidates) | reads | List small areas that stand out from their surroundings in colour or brightness, with box, size, colour difference to the surroundings, edge density and whether they touch the border. |
| [`measure_tilt`](#measure_tilt) | reads | Measure how far the long straight lines in a photo (horizon, walls, door frames) are from level and upright, as degrees with a confidence for the near-horizontal and the near-vertical group. |
| [`auto_correct`](#auto_correct) | writes | Run Lightroom's own Auto (the Auto button in the Basic panel) on each listed photo SEPARATELY: Lightroom looks at that photo alone and sets its exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites and blacks. |
| [`adjust_lighting`](#adjust_lighting) | writes | Change exposure and tone by the given amounts (relative to the current values). |
| [`adjust_white_balance`](#adjust_white_balance) | writes | Change white balance by the given amounts. |
| [`list_develop_parameters`](#list_develop_parameters) | reads | List the Lightroom develop parameters you can read and set with get_develop_parameters and set_develop_parameters (name, panel, allowed range). |
| [`get_develop_parameters`](#get_develop_parameters) | reads | Read the current value of develop settings of a photo (or its working copy). |
| [`set_develop_parameters`](#set_develop_parameters) | writes | Change listed develop parameters of a photo's virtual copy. |
| [`list_masks`](#list_masks) | reads | List the masks (local adjustments) on a photo or its working copy: how many, their names and the local adjustment values they carry. |
| [`create_mask`](#create_mask) | writes | Create a mask on the photo's virtual copy; it starts with no adjustments (use set_mask_adjustments next). |
| [`inspect_masks`](#inspect_masks) | reads | Show the masks of a photo's working copy as Lightroom reports them, including each mask's id (needed by set_mask_adjustments, invert_mask and delete_mask). |
| [`set_mask_adjustments`](#set_mask_adjustments) | writes | Change local adjustments inside ONE mask, so only the masked area changes. |
| [`invert_mask`](#invert_mask) | writes | Invert one mask so it covers everything it did not (for example: select the subject, then invert to adjust the background). |
| [`delete_mask`](#delete_mask) | writes | Delete one mask from the working copy (the original photo is never touched). |
| [`adjust_hsl`](#adjust_hsl) | writes | Change hue, saturation or luminance of single colours by the given amounts. |
| [`crop`](#crop) | writes | Set the crop box as fractions of the frame (0 = left/top edge, 1 = right/bottom edge). |
| [`get_tone_curve`](#get_tone_curve) | reads | Read a photo's tone curve as points on a 0-255 scale. |
| [`adjust_tone_curve`](#adjust_tone_curve) | writes | Set a tone curve on the photo's working copy (a virtual copy; never the original). |
| [`replace_background`](#replace_background) | writes | Cut out the subject and put it on a new background. |
| [`remove_objects`](#remove_objects) | writes | Remove objects, blemishes, dust or sensor spots by filling the given regions from their surroundings. |
| [`fix_red_eye`](#fix_red_eye) | writes | Remove red-eye (flash glow in pupils) inside the given eye boxes. |
| [`export_for_delivery`](#export_for_delivery) | writes | Export a photo, with its current edits and crop, as an sRGB JPEG into the exports folder (darkroom.toml [paths] exports_dir) under a name you choose. |
| [`list_snapshots`](#list_snapshots) | reads | List a photo's snapshots (named save points of its develop settings). |
| [`get_retouch_state`](#get_retouch_state) | reads | Read the spot-removal and red-eye corrections already on a photo (count and details). |
| [`get_ai_panel_state`](#get_ai_panel_state) | reads | Ask Lightroom what its AI panels report for a photo (Enhance, Reflection Removal, Remove panel, current tool). |
| [`list_keywords`](#list_keywords) | reads | List the keywords in the catalog as paths ('Places/Japan/Kyoto'), at most 500. |
| [`create_snapshot`](#create_snapshot) | writes | Save the working copy's current develop settings as a named snapshot (a save point you can come back to with restore_snapshot). |
| [`restore_snapshot`](#restore_snapshot) | writes | Put the working copy back to a snapshot's develop settings. |
| [`reset_develop`](#reset_develop) | writes | Reset the working copy's develop edits: everything ('all'), or one group (local masks, spot removal, crop, geometry transforms, red-eye). |
| [`remove_distracting_people`](#remove_distracting_people) | writes | Use Lightroom's own detection to find distracting people in the background and remove them (the Remove tool's 'distracting people'). |
| [`rotate_photo`](#rotate_photo) | writes | Rotate the working copy a quarter turn left or right (orientation, not the crop angle). |
| [`set_photo_metadata`](#set_photo_metadata) | writes | Set a photo's title, caption, headline, copyright or creator, and/or its colour label (red, yellow, green, blue, purple or none). |
| [`copy_develop_settings`](#copy_develop_settings) | writes | Copy chosen groups of develop settings from one photo to up to 10 others, giving them all the SAME values (use auto_correct instead when each photo should get values of its own). |
| [`find_photos`](#find_photos) | reads | Find photos in the whole catalog by rating, pick flag, colour label, keyword, file format, ISO or capture date. |
| [`create_smart_collection`](#create_smart_collection) | writes | Create a smart collection (a saved search that keeps itself up to date), for example all 4-star and better photos. |
| [`build_smart_previews`](#build_smart_previews) | writes | Build smart previews (small editable stand-ins) for up to 25 photos, so they can be edited while the original files are offline. |
| [`list_catalog_presets`](#list_catalog_presets) | reads | List the names of Lightroom's metadata presets (for example a copyright template) or file-naming presets. |
| [`apply_metadata_preset`](#apply_metadata_preset) | writes | Apply a metadata preset to photos. |
| [`enhance`](#enhance) | writes | Run Lightroom's AI Enhance on the working copy: 'denoise' (amount 1-100, RAW only) or 'superRes' (doubles the pixels). |
| [`reflection_removal`](#reflection_removal) | writes | Run Lightroom's AI Reflection Removal (for example glass glare) on the working copy. |
| [`undo`](#undo) | writes | Take back darkroom_ai's edits made in THIS session: the last one, or all of them. |
| [`get_library_state`](#get_library_state) | reads | Read a photo's star rating, pick/reject flag and keywords. |
| [`set_library_state`](#set_library_state) | writes | Set a photo's star rating, pick/reject flag and keywords (catalog data only). |
| [`undo_library_change`](#undo_library_change) | writes | Take back darkroom_ai's library changes (rating, flag, keywords) made in THIS session. |
| [`batch_set_library_state`](#batch_set_library_state) | writes | Set rating, pick/reject flag and keywords on several photos in one batch (up to 25). |
| [`batch_set_develop_parameters`](#batch_set_develop_parameters) | writes | Edit several photos in one batch (up to 10), each with its own values, on virtual copies. |
| [`undo_batch`](#undo_batch) | writes | Take back every change of one batch made in THIS session, by its batch_id. |
| [`list_presets`](#list_presets) | reads | List Lightroom's develop presets (name and folder). |
| [`apply_preset`](#apply_preset) | writes | Apply one of Lightroom's develop presets (a saved look) to the photo's virtual copy, by its exact name from list_presets. |
| [`get_preset`](#get_preset) | reads | Read what one develop preset contains WITHOUT applying it: every setting it would write, grouped by panel (tone, colour, detail, effects, curves, masks...), with values for plain settings and a short description for big ones (curves, masks). |
| [`try_presets`](#try_presets) | writes | Try up to 4 develop presets on the photo's working copy, one at a time: each is applied, measured on a real render (tones, clipping, colour, noise, chroma) and a preview of it is saved for you to look at, then the photo is put back exactly as it was. |
| [`get_preset_notes`](#get_preset_notes) | reads | Read the agent's own notes on presets (character, what each is best for, where to avoid it) and see which of Lightroom's presets have no note yet. |
| [`save_preset_note`](#save_preset_note) | reads | Save or update the agent's note about one Lightroom preset (its character, what it suits, where it goes wrong). |

### `get_app_status`

Reads only.

Check whether Lightroom Classic and Photoshop are running and ready to be used. Reads only: it never starts or closes anything. The connector block says which code this connector process runs and whether it is stale (older than the files on disk; restart it). States: ready; busy (a command runs or is stuck in Lightroom; the detail says how long); not_running; needs_user (running but not answering, e.g. a dialog is open; the next step says what to clear); not_installed; unknown.

No parameters.

### `get_capabilities`

Reads only.

Report the installed Lightroom Classic, plug-in and Photoshop versions, whether each is a version darkroom_ai was tested with, and which features are verified, untested, have a known issue or are unavailable. Reads only. Call it at the start of a session and before relying on an untested feature (for example RAW edits or people masks); tell the user about anything that is not 'verified' before you use it. An untested version is a warning, never a block.

No parameters.

### `run_selftest`

Reads only.

Check, probe by probe, that the installed Lightroom Classic (and Photoshop, if it is already running) still behaves as darkroom_ai expects: versions, catalog read, every Develop key the tools use (drift check), metadata, presets, preview. Run it after an Adobe update and report every probe. Reads only by default. With write=true it also makes ONE virtual copy in the test catalog, changes Exposure by +0.1 EV, reads it back and puts it back; that asks the user first. A failed probe means the matching tools may not work: say which.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `write` | boolean | no | `False` |  |

### `ensure_apps_running`

Reads only.

Start Lightroom Classic or Photoshop if it is not running, and wait until it answers. An app that is already running is never restarted. If it is running but not answering, you get state needs_user: tell the person what to clear, then call get_app_status until it says ready.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `app` | `lightroom` \| `photoshop` | yes |  |  |

### `get_photo_info`

Reads only.

Read facts about a photo and its current basic settings. Changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |

### `list_catalog_photos`

Reads only.

List photos in the open Lightroom catalog, one page at a time, with their ids and camera/lens/exposure facts. Reads only; changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `offset` | integer | no | `0` | How many photos to skip. min 0 |
| `limit` | integer | no | `25` | Most photos to return (1-100). min 1, max 100 |
| `path_contains` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos whose file path contains this text (e.g. a folder). |
| `include_virtual_copies` | boolean | no | `False` | Also list virtual copies (normally only the originals). |
| `min_rating` | integer (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos rated at least this (unrated counts as 0). |
| `max_rating` | integer (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos rated at most this (0 finds the unrated). |
| `flag` | `pick` \| `reject` \| `none` (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos with this flag. |
| `keyword` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos that have this keyword (any letter case). |
| `file_format` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos of this file format: RAW, DNG, JPG, TIFF, PSD or VIDEO. |
| `min_iso` | integer (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos at this ISO or higher. |
| `max_iso` | integer (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos at this ISO or lower. |
| `captured_from` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos captured on or after this date, written YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `captured_to` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos captured on or before this date, written YYYY-MM-DD. |

### `catalog_summary`

Reads only.

Summarise the whole catalog: how many photos, and counts by camera, lens, ISO band, file format, star rating, capture year and folder. Read only. Use it to understand a shoot or the library before editing, then list_catalog_photos to look at specific photos.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_photos` | integer | no | `2000` | min 50, max 10000 |
| `top` | integer | no | `10` | How many entries to list per group. min 3, max 30 |
| `path_contains` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos whose file path contains this text (a folder). |

### `list_catalogs`

Reads only.

List the Lightroom catalogs (.lrcat files) found on this PC, say which one is open now and which ones darkroom_ai is allowed to change. Reads file names, sizes and dates only; it never opens a catalog. folder (optional) also searches one more folder, two levels deep.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `folder` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | One more folder to search. |

### `get_catalog_info`

Reads only.

Describe the catalog that is open in Lightroom now: how many photos, virtual copies and keywords, the collection tree with counts, the folder tree with counts, whether darkroom_ai may change it, and which catalogs and photo folders the owner has allowed. Read only. Call it first in any catalog session, and again after the owner opens another catalog.

No parameters.

### `request_catalog_access`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Ask the OWNER to allow darkroom_ai to change a catalog (and optionally the photo folders it uses). The owner sees the full path and answers Yes or No; nothing is allowed on your say-so. The catalog must exist. Allowing a catalog does not open it: the owner still opens it in Lightroom (see get_catalog_info).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `catalog_path` | string | yes |  | Full path of the .lrcat file. min length 1 |
| `photo_folders` | list of string | no |  | Folders whose photos may be edited or imported in that catalog. max items 5 |

### `request_folder_access`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Ask the OWNER to allow darkroom_ai to import from and edit photos in a folder (for example the folder they just gave you). The owner sees the full path and answers Yes or No.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `folder` | string | yes |  | Full path of the folder. min length 1 |

### `create_collection_set`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Create a collection set (a folder for collections) in the open catalog. The path's last name is the new set; the sets before it must exist. Safe to repeat: an existing set is reused. Undo with undo_collection_change.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes |  | Name with "/" between levels, for example "Trips/Japan 2026". min length 1, max length 300 |

### `create_collection`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Create a collection in the open catalog. The path's last name is the new collection; the sets before it must exist (create_collection_set first). An existing collection is reused. Undo with undo_collection_change.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes |  | Name with "/" between levels, for example "Trips/Japan 2026". min length 1, max length 300 |

### `add_to_collection`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Add photos (masters or virtual copies) to an existing collection. Photos already in it are skipped. More than 10 new photos is a bulk change: the owner is asked for a go-ahead first. Undo with undo_collection_change.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `collection` | string | yes |  | Collection path such as "Trips/Japan". min length 1 |
| `photo_ids` | list of string | yes |  | min items 1, max items 200 |

### `remove_from_collection`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Remove photos from a collection (the photos stay in the catalog). Undo with undo_collection_change.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `collection` | string | yes |  | Collection path such as "Trips/Japan". min length 1 |
| `photo_ids` | list of string | yes |  | min items 1, max items 200 |

### `get_collection_photos`

Reads only.

List the photos in one collection (ids and file names, at most 200). Read only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `collection` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |
| `limit` | integer | no | `100` | min 1, max 200 |

### `create_keyword`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Create a keyword, or a keyword hierarchy ("Places/Japan/Kyoto"), in the catalog. Existing levels are reused. To put keywords on photos use set_library_state or batch_set_library_state. A created keyword cannot be deleted by darkroom_ai (remove it in Lightroom if needed).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes |  | Name with "/" between levels, for example "Trips/Japan 2026". min length 1, max length 300 |

### `undo_collection_change`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Take back darkroom_ai's collection changes made in THIS session (adds, removes, created collections and sets). scope "last" takes back the most recent one, "all" every one, newest first. A created collection or set is only deleted while it is empty.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scope` | `last` \| `all` | no | `last` |  |

### `scan_folder`

Reads only.

Say what importing a folder would add to the catalog (new photos, already-present photos, unsupported files) without changing anything. Always do this before import_folder.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `folder` | string | yes |  | Absolute folder path, inside the allowed folder. min length 1 |
| `recursive` | boolean | no | `False` | Include sub-folders. |

### `import_folder`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Add the photos in a folder to the catalog WITHOUT moving, copying or changing any file. This is a bulk change: the person is asked for a go-ahead showing how many photos will be added, so call scan_folder first and tell them. Adds at most max_files (50) new photos per call; call again for the rest. More than 10 photos needs the person's go-ahead. The list of added files is kept in the journal. It cannot be undone with the undo tool (the person removes the photos in Lightroom if needed).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `folder` | string | yes |  | Absolute folder path, inside the allowed folder. min length 1 |
| `recursive` | boolean | no | `False` | Include sub-folders. |
| `max_files` | integer | no | `50` | min 1, max 50 |

### `get_photo_metadata`

Reads only.

Read the camera, lens and exposure facts of a photo (make, model, lens, focal length, aperture, shutter speed, ISO, capture time, size, file type). Facts only; changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |

### `get_selected_photos`

Reads only.

List the photo(s) selected in Lightroom Classic, with their catalog ids. Reads only; changes nothing. Use the ids with the other tools.

No parameters.

### `find_photo`

Reads only.

Find a photo in the open catalog by its file path and return its catalog id. Reads only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes |  | Absolute path of the photo file. min length 1 |

### `get_preview`

Reads only.

Render the photo as Lightroom shows it right now and return the picture itself, so you can look at it. Use it to judge how the photo looks before and after an edit. Changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `long_edge` | integer | no | `1024` | Longest side of the picture in pixels (256-2048). min 256, max 2048 |

### `analyze_photo`

Reads only.

Export a small preview and measure it: tones, clipping, colour cast, faces if available.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |

### `analyze_batch`

Reads only.

Measure many photos in one call and return a few numbers per photo (tones, clipping, colour cast). Numbers only: no pictures, no faces, no verdicts. Use it to compare or group a large set cheaply before looking at individual photos. Reads only; changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_ids` | list of string | yes |  | Catalog ids to measure (1-25); repeats are ignored. min items 1, max items 25 |
| `long_edge` | integer | no | `512` | Longest side of the measured preview in pixels (256-1024). Smaller is faster. min 256, max 1024 |
| `time_budget_s` | number | no | `90.0` | Stop starting new photos after this many seconds; the rest are listed in not_processed so you can call again with them. min 1.0, max 300.0 |

### `measure_region`

Reads only.

Measure the colour and brightness of up to 6 rectangles of a photo as numbers (CIELAB lightness, a*, b*, hue angle, chroma, median RGB, clipping). Use it to check skin tone: look at the preview, put a small box on clean skin (cheek or forehead, away from hair, shadow edges and highlights), measure, change something, and measure the same boxes again. Pass two or more boxes to see how far apart they are. Reads only; changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `regions` | list of any | yes |  | min items 1, max items 6 |

### `plan_crop`

Reads only.

Work out the largest crop with a given shape (aspect ratio) that stays inside the picture after rotating it by `angle` degrees, as numbers for the `crop` tool. It changes nothing. To level a horizon: measure with measure_tilt, rotate by the opposite amount, plan the crop, apply it with `crop`, then measure again; if the tilt grew, use the other sign.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |
| `aspect` | string | no | `original` | 'original', or width:height such as 3:2, 4:5, 16:9, 1:1 (landscape or portrait is set by the order of the numbers). |
| `angle` | number | no | `0.0` | Rotation in degrees. min -45.0, max 45.0 |
| `anchor` | list of any (may be null) | no | `None` | [x, y] picture fractions to keep the crop near (for example a face), as far as the rotated picture allows. Omit to centre the crop. |

### `view_region`

Reads only.

Make a close-up picture of part of the photo as it is now, so you can look at it with your image viewer (for example a face, a shadow edge or a spot). Reads only.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |
| `box` | list of any | no | `[0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0]` | [x0, y0, x1, y1] as picture fractions. min items 4, max items 4 |
| `long_edge` | integer | no | `1024` | min 256, max 1600 |

### `zone_map`

Reads only.

Map brightness over the photo: a grid of cells (mean luma, tonal zone 0-10, clipping) and the connected dark regions with their box, area, how much darker than their surroundings they are, and how hard their edge is (a hard edge behind a subject is typical of flash shadows). Numbers only; look at the picture to decide what a region is. Reads only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |
| `rows` | integer | no | `6` | min 2, max 12 |
| `cols` | integer | no | `8` | min 2, max 16 |
| `shadow_luma` | number | no | `0.25` | Dark below this luma. |

### `find_candidates`

Reads only.

List small areas that stand out from their surroundings in colour or brightness, with box, size, colour difference to the surroundings, edge density and whether they touch the border. These are only measurements of what is different; they are not a list of things to remove. Look at the areas (view_region) before suggesting anything. Reads only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |
| `max_items` | integer | no | `8` | min 1, max 20 |

### `measure_tilt`

Reads only.

Measure how far the long straight lines in a photo (horizon, walls, door frames) are from level and upright, as degrees with a confidence for the near-horizontal and the near-vertical group. Positive means the content is rotated clockwise. It reports numbers only: look at the preview too, because a sloping street or a leaning building gives a false tilt. Reads only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |

### `auto_correct`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Run Lightroom's own Auto (the Auto button in the Basic panel) on each listed photo SEPARATELY: Lightroom looks at that photo alone and sets its exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites and blacks. Set white_balance to also run Auto White Balance. Values are never copied between photos. It edits each photo's working copy (a virtual copy; originals are never changed), limits every setting to the normal per-pass change, and reports what Lightroom chose and what was kept, with measurements before and after. More than one photo needs the person's go-ahead. `undo` takes back one photo; `undo_batch` takes back the batch. Lightroom must stay still while this runs (it switches to the Develop module for each photo).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_ids` | list of string | yes |  | min items 1, max items 25 |
| `tone` | boolean | no | `True` | Run Auto (exposure, contrast, tones). |
| `white_balance` | boolean | no | `False` | Also run Auto White Balance. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | `False` | Only show the plan; change nothing. |

### `adjust_lighting`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Change exposure and tone by the given amounts (relative to the current values). Values beyond the per-pass or total limits are clamped; the result lists what was applied.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `exposure` | number (may be null) | no | `None` | Change in EV; positive brightens, negative darkens. |
| `contrast` | number (may be null) | no | `None` | Change on the -100..100 scale. |
| `highlights` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `shadows` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `whites` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `blacks` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `allow_beyond_total` | boolean | no | `False` | Go beyond the total limit for this photo. Needs the user's confirmation. |

### `adjust_white_balance`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Change white balance by the given amounts. JPG/TIFF: both values are on Lightroom's relative -100..100 scale (positive temperature = warmer, positive tint = more magenta). RAW: temperature is a change in Kelvin. Values beyond the per-pass or total limits are clamped; the result lists what was applied.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `temperature` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `tint` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `allow_beyond_total` | boolean | no | `False` | Go beyond the total limit for this photo. Needs the user's confirmation. |

Reads only.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `panel` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Panel: basic, detail, lens, geometry, effects, color_grading, calibration. |

### `get_develop_parameters`

Reads only.

Read the current value of develop settings of a photo (or its working copy). Give the exact Lightroom setting names, e.g. "Clarity2012"; leave names empty for all listed parameters. Any Lightroom develop setting name can be read, not only the listed ones: for example the text settings in list_develop_parameters (readable_text_settings), such as LensProfileName, show whether Lightroom found a lens profile.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `names` | list of string | no |  | max items 80 |

### `set_develop_parameters`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Change listed develop parameters of a photo's virtual copy. Each value is the CHANGE to apply (positive or negative), not the final value; it is limited to the parameter's range and to a per-call amount. The original is never touched. Undo with the undo tool.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `changes` | object | yes |  |  |

### `list_masks`

Reads only.

List the masks (local adjustments) on a photo or its working copy: how many, their names and the local adjustment values they carry. Reads only; changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |

### `create_mask`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Create a mask on the photo's virtual copy; it starts with no adjustments (use set_mask_adjustments next). Positions are fractions of the picture as shown in Lightroom: x 0 = left, 1 = right; y 0 = top, 1 = bottom (the same fractions as in get_preview). - mask_type 'gradient': give start and end. The effect is full at start and fades to nothing at end. - mask_type 'radialGradient': give center, radius_x, radius_y (fractions of the width and height; the ellipse spans center +- radius), optional feather (0-100, default 50) and angle (degrees, default 0). The effect is inside the ellipse; use invert_mask for outside. - mask_type 'rangeMask' with subtype 'luminance': give luminance_range = four brightness values 0-1 in rising order (a, b, c, d): the mask ramps in from a to b, is full from b to c and ramps out from c to d (0, 0, 1, 1 = the whole tonal range). - mask_type 'aiSelection' with subtype subject, sky, background, objects or landscape. Lightroom switches to Develop while this runs; the person should not click in Lightroom meanwhile. - mask_type 'aiSelection' with subtype 'people': Lightroom only makes it after a person is chosen and 'Create Mask' is pressed in its panel, so the tool asks the person to do that, then waits up to a minute for the mask and checks it. - rangeMask color or depth cannot be created automatically yet. Undo with the undo tool.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |
| `mask_type` | `aiSelection` \| `rangeMask` \| `gradient` \| `radialGradient` | yes |  |  |
| `subtype` | string (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `start` | list of any (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `end` | list of any (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `center` | list of any (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `radius_x` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `radius_y` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `feather` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `angle` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `luminance_range` | list of any (may be null) | no | `None` |  |

### `inspect_masks`

Reads only.

Show the masks of a photo's working copy as Lightroom reports them, including each mask's id (needed by set_mask_adjustments, invert_mask and delete_mask). Lightroom switches to the Develop module while this runs. Changes nothing in the picture.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |

### `set_mask_adjustments`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Change local adjustments inside ONE mask, so only the masked area changes. Each value is the CHANGE to apply (positive or negative), not the final value, limited to the parameter's range and to a per-call amount (exposure 1.5 EV; others a quarter of their range). Names: see LOCAL_PARAMETERS in the error text if you use a wrong one. mask_id comes from create_mask or inspect_masks; leave it out to use the mask currently selected in Lightroom. Undo with the undo tool.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |
| `mask_id` | string (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `changes` | object | yes |  |  |

### `get_tone_curve`

Reads only.

Read a photo's tone curve as points on a 0-255 scale. Changes nothing. channel "rgb" is the combined curve; "red", "green" and "blue" are the colour curves. A straight line from (0,0) to (255,255) means no curve.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `channel` | `rgb` \| `red` \| `green` \| `blue` | no | `rgb` |  |

### `adjust_tone_curve`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Set a tone curve on the photo's working copy (a virtual copy; never the original). Give the whole curve as points on a 0-255 scale, from x=0 to x=255 with x increasing (2 to 16 points). Read the current curve first with get_tone_curve and change it a little: each output is limited to a small step from the current curve and to a bounded distance from a straight line, and outputs never fall below the point before. Anything limited is reported in `note`. channel "rgb" is the combined curve; "red", "green", "blue" are the colour curves. Undo with the ordinary undo tool.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `channel` | `rgb` \| `red` \| `green` \| `blue` | no | `rgb` |  |
| `points` | list of any | yes |  | min items 2, max items 16 |

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Cut out the subject and put it on a new background. Give `color` or `image`, not both.

### `remove_objects`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Remove objects, blemishes, dust or sensor spots by filling the given regions from their surroundings. The result is a NEW 16-bit TIFF and JPG (and a PSD with Content-Aware Fill on its own layer when Photoshop is used) made from the working copy as it is now; the original photo and the catalog are unchanged. 'content_aware' uses Photoshop and suits larger or textured objects; 'inpaint' works without Photoshop and suits small spots on smooth areas. Show the person what you intend to remove and get their agreement before calling this.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |
| `regions` | list of any | yes |  | min items 1, max items 8 |
| `method` | `auto` \| `content_aware` \| `inpaint` | no | `auto` |  |

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Remove red-eye (flash glow in pupils) inside the given eye boxes. The result is a NEW 16-bit TIFF and JPG made from the working copy as it is now; the original is unchanged. Only strongly red pixels inside the boxes change. Measure the eyes' share fixed in the result.

### `undo_library_change`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Take back darkroom_ai's library changes (rating, flag, keywords) made in THIS session. scope "last" takes back the most recent one; "all" takes back all of them on this photo. Keywords that were created are left in Lightroom's keyword list (only removed from the photo).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `scope` | `last` \| `all` | no | `last` |  |

### `batch_set_library_state`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Set rating, pick/reject flag and keywords on several photos in one batch (up to 25). Each item names a photo and its values (same rules as set_library_state: a master or a virtual copy, exactly the photo whose id you give). Everything is checked first; if any item is not allowed nothing runs. A batch of more than 5 photos needs the person's go-ahead, which this tool asks for itself. The run stops at the first failure and lists what was done, failed and not run. Use dry_run to see the plan without changing anything. Take a whole batch back with undo_batch.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | list of any | yes |  | min items 1, max items 25 |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | `False` | Only check and show the plan; change nothing. |

### `batch_set_develop_parameters`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Edit several photos in one batch (up to 10), each with its own values, on virtual copies. Each item gives changes for exposure and tone, white balance and/or other develop settings; every value goes through the same limits as adjust_lighting, adjust_white_balance and set_develop_parameters, and a master gets one new working copy (the plan says how many will be created). Always needs the person's go-ahead, which this tool asks for itself. Everything is checked first; the run stops at the first failure and lists what was done, failed and not run. Use dry_run to see the plan without changing anything. Take a whole batch back with undo_batch (settings are restored; created copies stay in the catalog).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | list of any | yes |  | min items 1, max items 25 |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | `False` | Only check and show the plan; change nothing. |

### `undo_batch`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Take back every change of one batch made in THIS session, by its batch_id. Restores settings and library fields from the journal and reads them back. Virtual copies a batch created are not deleted (deleting is never done). Changes made to the same photos after the batch are not separated out: the oldest recorded values are put back.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `batch_id` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |

### `list_presets`

Reads only.

List Lightroom's develop presets (name and folder). Reads only; changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `contains` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Only presets whose name or folder contains this text. |
| `limit` | integer | no | `100` | Most presets to return. min 1, max 500 |

### `apply_preset`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Apply one of Lightroom's develop presets (a saved look) to the photo's virtual copy, by its exact name from list_presets. The result lists every setting the preset changed, with before and after, so look at get_preview and judge it. A preset that moves exposure far from the original, or changes the crop or process version, is taken back automatically. Undo with the undo tool.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `preset_name` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |

### `get_preset`

Reads only.

Read what one develop preset contains WITHOUT applying it: every setting it would write, grouped by panel (tone, colour, detail, effects, curves, masks...), with values for plain settings and a short description for big ones (curves, masks). Give photo_id to also see, for each setting, what the photo has now. Use it to learn what a preset really does before choosing it. Changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `preset_name` | string | yes |  | Exact name from list_presets. min length 1 |
| `folder` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Folder, if the name is in several. |
| `photo_id` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Optional: compare with this photo's current values. |

### `try_presets`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Try up to 4 develop presets on the photo's working copy, one at a time: each is applied, measured on a real render (tones, clipping, colour, noise, chroma) and a preview of it is saved for you to look at, then the photo is put back exactly as it was. Use it to compare candidates before recommending one. Nothing stays changed; apply the chosen preset with apply_preset after the person agrees. A preset that changes framing or goes beyond the limits is reported as refused.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `preset_names` | list of string | yes |  | Exact preset names from list_presets (a name in several folders is refused). min items 1, max items 4 |

### `get_preset_notes`

Reads only.

Read the agent's own notes on presets (character, what each is best for, where to avoid it) and see which of Lightroom's presets have no note yet. Changes nothing in Lightroom.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `contains` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Only notes whose name, folder, tags or comment contain this. |
| `limit` | integer | no | `50` | min 1, max 200 |

### `save_preset_note`

Reads only.

Save or update the agent's note about one Lightroom preset (its character, what it suits, where it goes wrong). Keep it short and base it on the preset's name and folder or on a try_presets measurement. Writes only a small local notes file, never Lightroom.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `preset_name` | string | yes |  | Exact name from list_presets. min length 1 |
| `folder` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Folder, needed when the name exists in several folders. |
| `character` | list of string | no |  | max items 8 |
| `best_for` | list of string | no |  | max items 8 |
| `avoid_for` | list of string | no |  | max items 8 |
| `strength` | `subtle` \| `moderate` \| `strong` \| `unknown` | no | `unknown` |  |
| `comment` | string | no | `` | max length 600 |
| `evidence` | object | no |  |  |
